Maybe the goal is to make the gray bars form a "reflection" or "projection" of the yellow objects. Let me think about the vertical positions:

- Bottom yellow is at rows 33-37 (lower part of checkerboard)

- Bottom yellow (rows 33-37) -> projects to... where?
This doesn't make sense because the gray bars are below the checkerboard.
Let me think about the horizontal positions:
- Top yellow: cols 30-33 (center-right)
- Bottom yellow: cols 29-34 (center)
The gray bars span cols 20-42 (5 slots).
If I project the yellow objects horizontally onto the gray bar slots:
- Top yellow (cols 30-33) -> slots 3-4
- Bottom yellow (cols 29-34) -> slots 2-4

Top yellow shape: a cap (like "n"). If I project this onto 5 slots:
- Slots 1-2: no yellow
- Slot 3: yellow (left side of cap)
- Slot 4: yellow (right side of cap)
- Slot 5: no yellow
So the projection would be: slots 3-4 ON, slots 1-2-5 OFF.
Bottom yellow shape: a U with a bridge. If I project this onto 5 slots:
- Slot 1: no yellow
- Slot 2: yellow (left side of U)
- Slot 3: yellow (bridge and middle)
- Slot 4: yellow (right side of U)
- Slot 5: no yellow
So the projection would be: slots 2-3-4 ON, slots 1-5 OFF.
Now, how do I combine these two projections? Maybe:
- H bars represent the top yellow projection
- V bars represent the bottom yellow projection
So:
- H=ON at 3,4 (top yellow projection)
- V=ON at 2,3,4 (bottom yellow projection)
This is exactly what I just tried! And it didn't work.
Hmm, maybe I have the mapping reversed:
- H bars represent the bottom yellow projection
- V bars represent the top yellow projection
So:
- H=ON at 2,3,4 (bottom yellow projection)
- V=ON at 3,4 (top yellow projection)

- Turn OFF V at 2
